titulo: Unreal Past: I wish, if only, it's time
descripcion: At C2 the unreal past extends to its least intuitive forms: wish + would for a critique of someone else's ongoing behaviour, and as if / as though with a perfect form for a retrospective unreal comparison. The everyday uses are assumed known.

filas: I wish he would stop interrupting.
She spoke as if she had rehearsed it.
It's high time we addressed this properly.
cuadroReferencia.notaPie: Wish + would can never refer to the speaker's own action — I wish I would stop is not standard; use I wish I could stop instead.

ejemplos.texto: I wish he would stop interrupting every single meeting.
She spoke as if she had rehearsed every word in advance.
It's high time we addressed this properly, not just talked around it.

notas: Wish + would carries an implicit complaint about a repeated, controllable behaviour — it's rarely neutral.
As if/as though with the past perfect shifts the comparison into the past, distinguishing it from the simple past form used for a present comparison.
High time intensifies it's time and adds a stronger note of overdue reproach.

contraste.es: Spanish conveys the irritation of wish + would through tone or phrases like ya podría dejar de…, without a dedicated structure. Because English does have one, Spanish speakers at C2 tend to avoid it and fall back on wish + could, losing the note of complaint.
contraste.de: German has a close parallel in ich wünschte, du würdest… for complaining about someone else's behaviour, so wish + would feels natural. The difference is that German also allows ich wünschte, ich würde…, while English rules out I wish I would; as if + past perfect maps well onto als ob + Konjunktiv II Plusquamperfekt (als ob er es gesehen hätte).
contraste.it: Italian expresses the wish with vorrei che + congiuntivo imperfetto (vorrei che smettessi), without any would. Italian speakers therefore tend to write I wish you stopped and miss the note of complaint that wish + would carries; as if + past perfect maps well onto come se + congiuntivo trapassato (come se l'avesse visto).
contraste.fr: French uses j'aimerais que + subjonctif or si seulement + imparfait (si seulement tu arrêtais), which maps onto if only you stopped but not onto the note of complaint in wish + would. As if + past perfect is a direct match for comme si + plus-que-parfait (comme s'il l'avait vu).
contraste.pt: Portuguese expresses the wish with quem me dera que (European) or tomara que (Brazilian) plus the subjunctive, without any would. Portuguese speakers therefore tend to miss the note of complaint in wish + would; as if + past perfect maps well onto como se + mais-que-perfeito do conjuntivo (como se o tivesse visto).

errores: Using wish + would about the speaker's own action.
Using the simple past instead of the past perfect after as if for a retrospective comparison.
Treating it's time and it's high time as interchangeable in tone.

traducciones.pt: Já é mais do que tempo de…

redemittel.expresion: He acts as if nothing had happened.

traducciones.es: actúa como si nada hubiera pasado
traducciones.de: Er tut so, als wäre nichts passiert.
traducciones.fr: Il agit comme si rien ne s’était passé.
traducciones.it: Si comporta come se non fosse successo nulla.
traducciones.pt: Ele age como se nada tivesse acontecido.

autochequeo: Is wish + would used only about someone other than the speaker?
Is the past perfect used after as if for a retrospective comparison?
Does high time carry a stronger tone than plain time?
Does the sentence carry the implicit complaint that wish + would requires?
Would a native speaker read irritation here, or does it sound neutral by mistake?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on wish + would, as if/as though with the past perfect, and it's (high) time. Check the subject restriction on wish + would and the tense after as if. Do not rewrite the text.
